correctness.rationale: Writing U=X²,V=Y²,W=Z² and elementary symmetric functions, the cubic-coordinate Hessian identity reduces flex equations for smooth a to e1=1, e2=−1/(a−2), e3=−a/[3(a−2)²]. The squared coordinates are roots of P_a(T)=T³−T²−T/(a−2)+a/[3(a−2)²]. Independently expanded the Hessian syzygy and verified disc_T P_a=4(a−3)(a+1)²/[3(a−2)^4] and disc_a(3(a−2)²P_a)=−24T³+33T²−6T+1. The odd-degree parameter discriminant is nonsquare, making the cubic irreducible and its root-splitting group S3. At a=0 the cubic is separable with one simple zero root and independent valuations at its conjugate primes force two independent Kummer square classes, extending by degree 4 to the 24-point S4 regular cover. At a=0 one square-root sign flips (V4 double transposition); at a=3 two nonzero roots exchange (transposition); each order-two inertia fixes no point in the regular 24-element fiber, giving twelve simple ramification points. No assertion over excluded singular fibers or parameter infinity.
